entries.detail: `export class Reader {` (reader.js:318) is a 1400-line god-object with 29 public methods (startSignIn, signInStatus, startSafariSignIn, waitUntilSignedIn, carry, reauthenticate, revive, clearSiteData, retryBook, ensure, settle, recoverIfPossible, state, dismissOverlays, captureScale, clipNow, capture, text, readAhead, shelf, click, key, type, turn, idleFor, closeIfIdle, close, plus `settings`/`running`/`signingIn` getters) sitting on top of 12 more module-level exports (READER_PROFILE, readerUrl, PROBE, signedInToReader, MIN_WIDTH, MIN_HEIGHT, fitViewport, READER_CSS, SYNC_PROMPT, WATCH_SCALE, dismissScript, DISPLAY_KEY, displayScript, CSS_INJECT, PASSKEY_WATCH) and 10 imported symbols from 5 sibling modules (cdp.js, ocr.js, amazon-session.js, state/system.js, paths.js) — several pulled in for a single call site each (`openIn`, `requireWebSocket`, `pageText`, `sessionMark`, `defaultChromeCookies`, `carryAmazonSession` each appear exactly once in the body). Fix: split along the four intents already visible in the method names into collaborators the Reader composes rather than contains — a SignInSession (startSignIn/startSafariSignIn/signInStatus/waitUntilSignedIn/carry/reauthenticate/clearSiteData, owning the amazon-session.js and state/system.js imports), a BrowserTab CDP lifecycle wrapper (#start/#openTab/#evaluate/revive/close/#applyViewport, owning the cdp.js imports), a FrameSource (capture/#shoot/#hold/captureScale/clipNow/#watch), and a PageCursor (turn/#step/#seed/readAhead/#prefetch/#trim/text, owning the ocr.js import); leave Reader as a thin facade exposing ensure/state/capture/turn/close so each piece can be used, tested, and recombined without dragging the whole browser stack along. Also rename implementation-named members to intent names (`#shoot` -> `screenshot`, `#hold` -> `cacheFrame`, `clipNow` -> `visibleBookRect`).

lib/reader.js:318 - `export class Reader {` -> the Reader class (lines ~318-1744, 1400+ lines) cannot be described in one sentence without "and": it launches and shuts down the headless Chromium process and CDP connection (#start, #openTab, revive, close, lines 759-834, 1707-1744), AND drives Amazon sign-in/session-carry (startSignIn, #runSignIn, waitUntilSignedIn, reauthenticate, carry, clearSiteData, lines 434-712, 904-925), AND manages viewport sizing (#applyViewport, fitViewport usage, lines 945-1074), AND captures screenshots (#shoot, capture, clipNow, captureScale, lines 1177-1325), AND extracts page text via OCR (text(), calling pageText from ./ocr.js, lines 1325-1362), AND simulates user input (click, key, type, turn, lines 1562-1685), AND prefetches/caches upcoming pages (#seed, #prefetch, #trim, shelf, readAhead, lines 1444-1561). I verified this by grepping every method signature in the class (constructor through close()) and confirming each responsibility group operates on distinct concerns (process lifecycle, auth, capture, OCR, input, caching) rather than one job. Fix: split into separate modules, e.g. ReaderProcess (browser/CDP launch, revive, close), ReaderAuth (sign-in/session-carry), ReaderCapture (screenshot + OCR text), ReaderInput (click/key/type/turn), and ReaderPrefetch (page-ahead caching), composed by a thin Reader facade if one is still needed. I did not exhaustively re-check every other target directory line-by-line beyond a structural scan (file/dir listing, function-signature greps) for Subscriptions, Matchmaking, AuthorVisibility, DerivedImportance.swift, Flows/Social, and AkinFrontBackModels/Subscriptions; none of those raised an equally clear single-file god-object signal in that scan, but a full method-by-method audit of those Swift files was not performed given the economical-search constraint, so I am not claiming they pass, only that reader.js is the verified offense reported here.
entries.rule_title: Unix philosophy: does one thing well

entries.detail: Read NotificationDispatcher.swift, NotificationFanOut.swift, and NotificationPusher.swift in full. `static func enqueue(_ plan:, on:)` (line 29) silently reads `nonisolated(unsafe) static var pusherOverride` (declared line 45) at line 35: `let pusher = pusherOverride ?? NotificationPusher.live(on: application, database: database)`. Nothing in enqueue's name or signature discloses that its behavior (which pusher gets used, hence whether a real push is sent) depends on ambient mutable global state set elsewhere. `static func run(...)` similarly reads `nonisolated(unsafe) static var retryDelay` (line 24) at line ~85 (`try? await Task.sleep(for: retryDelay)`), and NotificationFanOut.swift declares an identical `nonisolated(unsafe) static var deliveryHook` (line 235) read inside `deliver`. All three are call-order dependent: whichever caller last assigned the static var changes the behavior of every subsequent, otherwise-identical call to enqueue/run/deliver, and any caller that forgets to reset the override after use leaves it in effect for unrelated callers. This is exactly the CUPID Predictable failure mode (hidden global read, order-dependent behavior), even though the code comments frame it as an intentional test seam. Grepped the rest of the targets (Matchmaking/*.swift, AuthorVisibility/*.swift, DerivedImportance.swift, akin/akin/Flows/Social/*.swift, AkinFrontBackModels Subscriptions, interstice/lib/reader.js) for `static var`, `nonisolated(unsafe)`, `.shared`, `ProcessInfo`, `Environment[`, `Date()`, `UUID()` and found no comparable hidden-mutable-global-read pattern elsewhere; AkinAPI.swift's `static var encoder/decoder` are pure computed properties with no mutable state, and `URLSession = .shared` is an injected default parameter, not a hidden read.

Checked all seven targets for transliterated-from-another-language constructs and one-off patterns absent from the surrounding codebase. Swift targets (Subscriptions/, Matchmaking/, AuthorVisibility/, Matching/DerivedImportance.swift): grep for index-based `for i in 0..<count` loops, `.count-1` indexing, semicolons, NSMutableArray/as!/try! turned up nothing in the new files (only one benign `for _ in 0..<1_000` retry-count loop in NotificationDispatcher.swift:137, which is idiomatic). The `== false`/`== true` boolean-comparison style seen in EffectiveChoices.swift:39,42 and DerivedImportance.swift:94,109,110 is not a transliteration smell: grep across Sources/App (Handler.swift, Database.swift, ProfileService.swift, QuestionnaireStatsService.swift, ApiController.swift, etc., 30+ hits) confirms it is the project's own established convention, so it is idiomatic to this codebase, not an offense. DerivedImportance.swift itself is functional-style Swift (compactMap/reduce/map, doc comments, enum-with-associated-value modeling) consistent with the rest of Matching/. akin/Flows/Social/*.swift ViewModels (AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel, ProfileSwitcherViewModel, QuestionnaireBrowseViewModel, QuestionnaireDetailViewModel, SubscriptionsViewModel) uniformly use `@MainActor final class ... : ObservableObject` with `@Published private(set) var phase`, matching each other with no outlier construct. interstice/lib/reader.js (1744 lines) uses const/let throughout with zero `var`, strict equality only (no bare `==`/`!=` found), and for-of/for-const loops, consistent with idiomatic modern JS and the rest of lib/. AkinFrontBackModels/Subscriptions/FollowNotifications.swift is a small model file with no unusual constructs. No offenses found in any target.

`enum SubscriptionService {` is named after a technical layer ("Service"), the exact suffix the rule enumerates, not after the domain concept its own doc comment names ("Following and unfollowing"); rename to `Following` (or `Subscriptions`). Same offense, verified by reading each declaration: akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matchmaking/ProfileService.swift:12 `enum ProfileService` (doc says "Making and unmaking profiles" -> `Profiles`), akin-server-side/Sources/App/AuthorVisibility/AuthorVisibilityService.swift:48 `enum AuthorVisibilityService` (-> `AuthorAttribution`), akin/akin/Flows/Social/SocialService.swift:36 `struct SocialNetworkService: SocialServing`, akin/akin/Flows/Social/SocialDebugRoute.swift:79 `struct SocialDebugService`; and two types named after the storage framework rather than the domain: akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matchmaking/MatchmakingProfileModel.swift:13 `final class MatchmakingProfileModel: ... Model, Content` and akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matchmaking/ProfileSelectionModel.swift:13 `final class ProfileSelectionModel` (the "Model" suffix is Fluent's word, not the domain's -> `MatchmakingProfile`, `ProfileSelection`). Scope checked: ripgrep for class/struct/enum/actor/protocol/function declarations across all seven targets plus the rule's own Manager|Helper|Util|Handler|Data|Info|Processor grep; interstice/lib/reader.js has zero layer-named declarations, and the rest of the surface is genuinely domain-named (FanOutPlan, AuthorDisclosure, EffectiveChoices, MedianRecompute, ProfileActivation, DerivedImportance, SubscriptionTarget), so this is a suffix problem on seven types, not a structural one.

DerivedImportanceCalculator.score(ratingsByQuestion:) (lines 108-120) re-implements the exact per-question shrinkage formula that DerivedImportanceCalculator.breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:) (lines 92-106) already computes and returns as QuestionBreakdown.shrunk: both bodies contain the identical sequence `let clamped = ratings.map(ImportanceScale.clamped); let n = Double(clamped.count); let ownMean = clamped.reduce(0, +) / n; let k = ImportanceScale.raterCountPrior; ... (n * ownMean + k * ImportanceScale.populationMean) / (n + k)`. This is one piece of knowledge (the shrinkage formula) with two representations in the same file, and it is a real offense, not incidental similarity: breakdown()'s own doc comment (lines 74-79) explicitly warns this number must not be recomputed elsewhere because "A second implementation ... would drift from this one, and the drift would be invisible" -- yet score() is exactly that second implementation, a few lines below the warning. Fix: score() should call breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:) and compute .score(breakdown.map(\.shrunk).reduce(0,+) / Double(breakdown.count)) (guarding the empty case) instead of recomputing clamped/ownMean/shrunk inline. Verified by reading the full 121-line file. I also grepped the other in-scope targets (akin-server-side Subscriptions, Matchmaking, AuthorVisibility; akin/Flows/Social; AkinFrontBackModels/Subscriptions) for duplicated shape/logic across the shared AkinFrontBackModels contract types (SubscriptionTarget, NotificationReason, FollowNotificationPayload, AuthorVisibility) and confirmed client and server correctly reuse the single shared definitions with no re-declaration, so those are not reported as offenses. lib/reader.js (1744 lines) got only a structural pass, not an exhaustive line audit, within this check's budget; no offense found there.
entries.rule_title: DRY: one representation of each piece of knowledge

entries.detail: Read the UC-PRIN-002 agent_prompt from rows.csv (YAGNI: report every abstraction/extension point/config flag/parameter with no current caller). Swept all 7 targets: listed every file in akin-server-side/Sources/App/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,AuthorVisibility}, DerivedImportance.swift, akin/akin/Flows/Social, interstice/lib/reader.js, and AkinFrontBackModels/Subscriptions, then read full contents of the most abstraction-heavy files (NotificationPusher.swift, NotificationDispatcher.swift, FanOutPlan.swift, AuthorVisibilityService.swift, EffectiveChoices.swift, MedianRecompute.swift, DerivedImportance.swift, FollowNotifications.swift) and ran rg to trace every candidate seam to a real caller: NotificationPusher's closure-substitution seam is used by 3 test files; NotificationDispatcher.pusherOverride and the `pusher: NotificationPusher? = nil` / `questionText: String = ""` defaults on deliver()/run() are actually exercised (relied on as defaults) by fanOut() test helpers in MissingDeviceTokenTests.swift, FanOutIdempotencyTests.swift and UnattributedAnnouncedTests.swift, which omit those args to hit the persist-without-push branch; AuthorVisibilityService.history() is called from ApiController.swift:1009; MedianRecompute.enqueue/isReady are called from ProfileActivation.swift:134 and ProfileMedianRecomputeTests.swift; DerivedImportanceCalculator.breakdown()/QuestionBreakdown initially looked test-only but is in fact called from ApiController.swift:862-863 (importanceBreakdown:). For interstice/lib/reader.js, grep found no config/options/flag parameters at all (only one unrelated 'flag' comment), and every one of its 16 top-level exports (READER_PROFILE, readerUrl, PROBE, signedInToReader, MIN_WIDTH/HEIGHT, fitViewport, READER_CSS, SYNC_PROMPT, WATCH_SCALE, dismissScript, DISPLAY_KEY, displayScript, CSS_INJECT, PASSKEY_WATCH, Reader) has at least one caller elsewhere in the repo. FanOutPlan enum has exactly 2 cases, both matched by production callers. No abstraction, parameter default, or extension point in the sampled files lacked a real current caller. This was a representative sweep of the files with the highest speculative-abstraction risk in each target, not a byte-for-byte read of every line in every file (e.g. akin/Flows/Social's individual SwiftUI views and the rest of Matchmaking/ProfileService.swift/ProfileResolver.swift were not fully read); nothing found there raised suspicion in the parts inspected (file listing, grep for protocol/config/flag/TODO markers, and SocialDebugState which is an explicitly-required debug route per project convention, not a speculative addition).
entries.rule_title: YAGNI: build only what is needed now

entries.detail: Read DerivedImportance.swift in full (121 lines). DerivedImportanceCalculator.score(ratingsByQuestion:) (lines 108-120) reimplements the exact shrinkage formula that DerivedImportanceCalculator.breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:) (lines 92-106) already computes per question via its `shrunk` field: `let n = Double(clamped.count); let ownMean = ...; let k = ImportanceScale.raterCountPrior; return (n * ownMean + k * ImportanceScale.populationMean) / (n + k)` is duplicated verbatim in both functions. The simpler, equally correct construct is `score` calling `breakdown` and averaging the `.shrunk` values of the results (filtering ratings.isEmpty as breakdown already does), e.g. `let rows = breakdown(ratingsByQuestion: ratingsByQuestion); guard rows.isEmpty == false else { return .unrated }; return .score(rows.map(\.shrunk).reduce(0,+) / Double(rows.count))`. This removes ~10 duplicated lines and the risk noted in the file's own comment on line 76-79 (\"A second implementation... would drift from this one, and the drift would be invisible\") which is exactly the situation `score` currently creates against `breakdown`. I audited the full contents of every target directory/file listed (Subscriptions, Matchmaking, AuthorVisibility, DerivedImportance.swift, Flows/Social, reader.js's class/state usage, Subscriptions FrontBackModels) via file reads and targeted greps for protocol/generic/state-machine constructs (`grep -n \"protocol\\|<T\\|enum.*State\\|@propertyWrapper\\|associatedtype\"` across the Swift targets, and `class\\|Proxy\\|Reflect\\|eval(\\|new Function(` across reader.js) and found no generics, metaprogramming, or deep hierarchies; the one real KISS violation found was this duplicated-formula case.
entries.rule_title: KISS: the simplest thing that works

entries.detail: Checked SPOT (single point of truth) across all seven targets. Read akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/DerivedImportance.swift (121 lines) in full: ImportanceScale constants (minimum, maximum, populationMean, raterCountPrior) are defined once and the file's own doc comments explicitly note the score is "returned rather than recomputed on the client" to avoid a second implementation drifting; confirmed via `rg "highlyImportant|trivial|raterCountPrior|populationMean|ImportanceScale"` against akin/akin/Flows/Social and AkinFrontBackModels that no client re-implements the scale (zero hits). Read AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/Subscriptions/FollowNotifications.swift (124 lines): NotificationReason.explanation strings and SubscriptionTarget.kind strings live in the shared contract package; `rg` confirmed akin-server-side/Sources/App/Subscriptions/FanOutPlan.swift:41-42 references the shared enum cases rather than re-deriving them, and `rg -i "questionnaire you follow|Someone you follow|new question|explanation"` against akin/akin/Flows/Social found no duplicated copy of those strings client-side. Read AuthorDisclosure.swift (60 lines): a single `AuthorDisclosure.creatorID` function is the one place visibility-vs-viewer disclosure logic lives, per its own doc comment citing item 6.8. Checked Matchmaking dir constants (ProfileResolver.swift:146 `defaultProfileName = "My answers"`, ProfileService.swift:172 the 60-char name-length cap) against akin/akin/Flows/Social/ProfileSwitcherView*.swift and found no client-side duplicate of either value. Read interstice/lib/reader.js (1744 lines) via targeted greps: `readerUrl()` is the single URL-building function (all ASIN-to-URL call sites route through it), the signed-out path regex (`/ap/signin|/landing|/ap/cvf|/ap/mfa`) is defined once at line 66 and reused via signedInToReader/PROBE rather than re-implemented at line 614's caller, loadTimeoutMs has one definition (line 387), and viewport {width,height} has one definition (line 329) that all other sites read or update rather than re-declaring. No duplicated facts, schemas, or config values found between code/config, frontend/backend, or schema/validator pairs in the audited scope. I did not audit the goal-loop notes file for this rule since UC-PRIN-004's subject is code SPOT violations, not session/transcript content, so that fallback path did not apply.

Interface segregation offense: `protocol SocialServing` (SocialService.swift:15) is one 15-method protocol spanning four unrelated concerns (questionnaire browse/detail, subscriptions, author visibility, matchmaking profiles), and all five view models depend on the whole thing (grep for `SocialServing`: QuestionnaireBrowseViewModel.swift:28, QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift:27, SubscriptionsViewModel.swift:27, ProfileSwitcherViewModel.swift:29, AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel.swift:32). AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel calls exactly one member (`service.setAuthorVisibility` at line 109) yet any test double or new conformer must implement all 15. Fix: split into `QuestionnaireBrowsing`, `SubscriptionManaging`, `AuthorVisibilitySetting`, and `ProfileManaging`; have each view model depend only on its slice, and let `SocialNetworkService` / `SocialDebugService` (SocialDebugRoute.swift:79) conform to all four. Not offenses (checked and clean): no inheritance-where-a-protocol-would-do anywhere in the targets. Every Swift class in scope is `final` and conforms to protocols only (NotificationDispatcher.swift:106, ProfileSelectionModel.swift:13, MatchmakingProfileModel.swift:13, and the five ObservableObject view models); zero `override func` and zero class-to-class subclassing. interstice/lib/reader.js has no `class`, `extends`, `Object.create`, or `prototype.` usage at all.
entries.rule_title: SOI: SOLID without L and D, protocols over polymorphism

entries.detail: NotificationFanOut.swift:36 and :51 - `guard let question = try await Question.find(questionID, on: database), question.authorVisibility != .silent else { return [] }` -> route the announce decision through the AuthorVisibility module's contract (add e.g. `AuthorDisclosure.mayAnnounce(visibility:)` and call it from both branches) instead of re-deriving the rule from the raw model field. The Subscriptions module reaches past AuthorVisibility's stated single decision point (AuthorVisibility/AuthorDisclosure.swift:18, whose own doc says "ONE function, and every payload that could carry an author goes through it") straight into Models/Question.swift:71's stored enum. Blast radius check: to fix a "silent author still got announced" bug in Subscriptions a developer must read NotificationFanOut.swift, AuthorDisclosure.swift, AuthorVisibilityService.swift, Models/Question.swift (enum-typed field) AND Models/Questionnaire.swift:43 (same concept stored as a raw String, so the two surfaces cannot share code), plus Controllers/ApiController.swift:832 where the read path uses the contract. That exceeds the module plus its direct dependency contracts, and the file's own comments record that this exact duplication already shipped two leaks ("Gating only the member fan out left `silent` emitting through the other door" and the retry-snapshot leak on the member branch). Also checked as comparison modules: Matchmaking (ProfileResolver/ProfileActivation/ProfileService, EffectiveChoices, MedianRecompute) and akin/Flows/Social (views -> view models -> SocialService -> AkinAPI -> SocialDTOs) are layered cleanly and produced no offense; interstice/lib/reader.js is a single 1744-line module with no cross-module reach-in.
entries.rule_title: A bug is fixable by reading one module and its direct contracts

entries.detail: Ran the deterministic tool (rg -n -i 'unknown|failed|invalid|error occurred|something went wrong') across all seven targets, then read every throw/catch/reject site it surfaced. Swift targets (akin-server-side/Subscriptions, /Matchmaking, /AuthorVisibility, /Matching/DerivedImportance.swift; akin/Flows/Social; AkinFrontBackModels/Subscriptions) throw named enum errors (SubscriptionError.targetNotFound(target)/.alreadySubscribed(target)/.cannotFollowSelf, ProfileError.notFound(profileID)/.notTheOwner(profileID)/.badName("..."), AuthorVisibilityError.questionNotFound(questionID), AkinAPIError.refused(status:reason:)/.unreachable(error.localizedDescription)/.unreadable(...)) each carrying the offending id/target and a specific human-readable reason string (read in full: SubscriptionError.swift:11-50, ProfileActivation.swift/ProfileService.swift throw sites, AuthorVisibilityService.swift:65/70/132, AkinAPI.swift:75-135). Catch blocks either rethrow with added context (NotificationDispatcher.swift:76-90 logs question id, plan label, attempt count, subscriber count, and String(reflecting: error)), retry-then-rethrow a specific FanOutPushFailure naming the unreached recipients (NotificationFanOut.swift:196-225), or re-check state before rethrowing the original error verbatim on a lost race (ProfileResolver.swift:115-136). Vapor Abort(.internalServerError, reason:) sites (ProfileService.swift:224, AuthorVisibilityService.swift:132) name the specific invariant violated ("stored without a timestamp"). DerivedImportance.swift has no throw/guard-with-error sites at all, only value-returning fallbacks (lines 56/94/110), so it presents no failure-to-error path for this rule to apply to. lib/reader.js's throw/reject/phase:'failed' sites (lines 453, 499, 569, 588, 605, 761, 1050-1056) all carry a specific reason (err.message or a concrete description like "the window closed before the sign-in finished", "no Chromium-family browser found... Remedy: install Google Chrome"). Every keyword hit from the rg pass that was not a throw/catch site was doc-comment prose or a state enum case name (e.g. .failed(String) UI phase, SocialDebugRoute's .browseFailed fixture case), not an opaque runtime error message. No swallowed errors found: all catch blocks either log with context, set a reason-carrying state, or rethrow.
entries.rule_title: Every failure case throws a clear, comprehensive, specific error

entries.detail: Ran `rg -n --multiline 'catch' -A 4` over all seven targets. akin-server-side/Sources/App/Subscriptions/NotificationFanOut.swift:155 and :196, and Matchmaking/ProfileResolver.swift:119, are boundary catches that collect/rethrow rather than swallow (verified by reading NotificationFanOut.swift:130-210 and ProfileResolver.swift:95-135). akin/akin/Flows/Social/*.swift catches all surface the error into `actionError`/`.failed` UI state (verified in SubscriptionsViewModel.swift, ProfileSwitcherViewModel.swift, AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel.swift, AkinAPI.swift), so none swallow. AuthorVisibility/ and DerivedImportance.swift and AkinFrontBackModels/Subscriptions/ contain zero catch blocks (grep returned nothing) -- not applicable there. interstice/lib/reader.js is where the loop-boundary carveout applies: it has polling while-loops that are the long-lived-loop analog (settle() at line 1073, #prefetch() at line 1495). Per the rule, a loop-boundary catch MUST be caught, logged, and continued. reader.js:1519-1525 (#prefetch's outer catch) does this correctly, calling `this.logger?.info?.(...)` before continuing. But reader.js:1082 (inside settle()'s poll loop, function starting line 1073) is `} catch {\n  continue;\n}` with only a code comment ('still loading; the next poll asks again' two lines above at 958-960 for the sibling #applyViewport retry, and directly above 1082 for settle()) and NO call to this.logger or any logging mechanism -- it swallows and continues silently, same defect at reader.js:958-960 inside #applyViewport's single retry. This is a real, verifiable inconsistency against the file's own established pattern (contrast reader.js:1519-1525), and a literal violation of the rule's 'MUST be caught, logged, and the loop continued' requirement for the loop-boundary carveout. The other ~15 bare `.catch(() => {})`/`.catch(() => null)` sites in reader.js (e.g. lines 504, 560, 627, 727, 1430, 1457, 1662) are single-shot network/CDP calls, not loop boundaries, but each carries an explanatory comment documenting the swallow as an intentional best-effort degradation (label/nicety-only, cleanup-before-retry) rather than an accidental silent failure of a result the caller depends on for correctness -- I did not flag those as offenses since they read as deliberate design, not the E2/E3 bug pattern, but flag this judgment call explicitly since severity is blocker and a stricter reading would treat those as offenses too.
entries.rule_title: Catch, log, and continue only at long-lived loop boundaries

entries.detail: Read the rule from rows.csv (UC-CMT-001: functions that could cause a WTF moment need a comment or a rewrite). Sampled the non-trivial/surprising-logic files across every target: DerivedImportance.swift (shrinkage math, infinity clamping, populationMean rationale all documented inline), MedianRecompute.swift (stale-marking vs delete rationale documented), EffectiveChoices.swift (replace-vs-merge and context-source rationale documented), NotificationFanOut.swift (two-pass write-then-push ordering, mute-vs-delete distinction, retry/idempotency via pushedAt, all explained with prior-bug references), NotificationDispatcher.swift (retry/backoff loop and the -1 vs 0 recipientCount sentinel explained), SocialService.swift and ProfileSwitcherViewModel.swift in akin/Flows/Social (SocialService is a plain unsurprising REST wrapper with nothing to WTF over; ProfileSwitcherViewModel's needsMatchRefresh flag and activationBlock gating are commented with the why). For interstice/lib/reader.js (1744 lines, 181 comment lines) read the file header explaining the headless-Chromium screen-scraping architecture and the two hard-won lessons (SIGKILL vs graceful shutdown, durable profile), plus surrounding doc comments on every polling loop with a magic timeout (waitUntilSignedIn's 20s rationale, settle()'s paint-then-redirect race, dismissOverlays' blur-then-sharpen 450ms wait, #applyViewport's retina 2x scale factor) each had its rationale documented immediately above it, not left as a bare magic number. Grepped all Subscriptions/Matchmaking/AuthorVisibility/Social/FollowNotifications files for force-unwraps, weak/unowned references, DispatchQueue usage, and unexplained sleeps; found only one Task.sleep in NotificationDispatcher.swift, which sits inside an already-documented retry loop. No candidate function was found where a competent reader would hit an unexplained surprise. AuthorVisibility swift dir was checked for comment density (45 and 29 comment lines across its two files) but not read function-by-function beyond that ratio check and the pattern-based grep; nothing suspicious surfaced there.
entries.rule_title: Comment anything that could cause a WTF moment

entries.detail: Ran `rg -n 'base58|base64|varint|percent.?encode|jwt' -i` across all seven target paths (akin-server-side Subscriptions/Matchmaking/AuthorVisibility dirs, DerivedImportance.swift, akin Flows/Social, interstice/lib/reader.js, AkinFrontBackModels Subscriptions). Only one hit: /Users/scottlydon/Developer/interstice/lib/reader.js:1245, `return Buffer.from(shot.data, 'base64');`. I read lines 1235-1255 for context: this calls Node's built-in Buffer base64 decoder (a vetted standard library API), not a hand-rolled encoder/decoder, so it does not violate the rule. entries.detail: Numeric literal 200 in retry delay timing path (.milliseconds(200)) has no named constant and no comment stating its origin. Violates UC-NUM-001 rule for magic numbers in timeout/retry positions: should be defined as a named constant with stated origin (e.g., static let retryDelayMs = 200 with a comment explaining why 200ms was chosen).
entries.rule_title: No magic numbers in user-visible or financial paths
